goal: Implicit scope dependencies between overlapping batch children follow a topological order of the declared blocked_by edges, with Slice order only breaking ties, so a plan whose declared dependencies are acyclic never projects a cycle when a higher-numbered Slice (such as branch-boundary-r2 S10) is a declared prerequisite of lower-numbered overlapping Slices; batch authorization, Lane admission and parked-child skipping keep using the same edges.

acceptance.assertion: projectParallelGroups and startableChildren accept a plan whose declared blocked_by edges are acyclic but whose Slice order disagrees with them: children S2 (blocked_by S10), S3 (blocked_by S2, S10), S4 (no declared dependency) and S10 (no declared dependency), all with overlapping scope_hint, project the waves [S4], [S10], [S2], [S3] without throwing, and every implicit edge points from a child placed earlier in that order to one placed later.

When declared dependencies leave two overlapping children unordered, the lower Slice still runs first (a child without slice_id keeps its list position); a declared dependency cycle is still rejected with the acyclic error; blockedByParked still skips a later overlapping child and its dependents behind a parked child.
The committed Claude MCP bundle matches the runtime source.
